statements.status_notes: GO-2026-5932 is a categorical advisory that golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained and unsafe by design, affecting all versions with no fix. The package is vendored only through Helm's pkg/provenance chart-signature verification. The console does reach that path by default: its chart-verifier integration (pkg/helm/chartverifier) runs the SignatureIsValid check, which routes through action.NewVerify().Run -> downloader.VerifyChart -> pkg/provenance -> openpgp.CheckDetachedSignature. But the check is guarded by an `if len(opts.PublicKeys) > 0` test that returns a Skipped result when no public key is configured, and the console never configures one — it sets only the vendor-type profile and a /tmp repository cache, and the verifier request carries no key field — so opts.PublicKeys is always empty and the openpgp code is never executed.

CVE-2026-48978 lets a malicious OCI registry redirect the oras-go auth client's Bearer-challenge realm to exfiltrate the caller's registry credentials and refresh tokens in cleartext. oras-go v1 is reached only through Helm's OCI registry client, which the console constructs with no authentication (pkg/helm/actions GetOCIRegistry sets no credentials): its chart pulls are anonymous, so the credential-bearing token exchange the advisory hijacks is never performed and there is no stored secret for a rogue realm to leak. The issue is LOW severity (CVSS 2.1) with no fixed oras-go v1 release; the separately-vendored oras-go v2 module carries the fix and is pinned to 2.6.2 here.

CVE-2024-7631 is a path traversal in the console's /locales/resource.json handler: the lng and ns query parameters were joined into a served filesystem path, letting a request with ../ segments read arbitrary .json files off the pod. The committed patch package/main/openshift-console/patch/i18n-locales-path-traversal-4.22.patch rejects any lng or ns containing a path separator or ".." before the join and returns HTTP 400, so the vulnerable traversal path is no longer present in the shipped bridge. Verified against the built image: a legitimate request (lng=en, ns=public) still returns the locale file with 200, while the traversal PoC (lng=../../../docker/sbom, ns=.spdx) and its URL-encoded variant are both rejected with 400.

CVE-2024-6508 is insufficient entropy in the OAuth2 login state parameter, which weakened the CSRF protection of the authorization flow. The shipped bridge generates the state from 16 bytes (128 bits) of crypto/rand read via io.ReadFull and hex-encodes it (pkg/auth/oauth2 LoginFunc), so the low-entropy implementation the advisory describes is not present.

GO-2026-5932 is a categorical advisory that golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained and unsafe by design, affecting all versions with no fix. The package is vendored only through Helm's pkg/provenance chart-signature verification. The console does reach that path by default: its chart-verifier integration (pkg/helm/chartverifier) runs the SignatureIsValid check, which routes through action.NewVerify().Run -> downloader.VerifyChart -> pkg/provenance -> openpgp.CheckDetachedSignature. But the check is guarded by an `if len(opts.PublicKeys) > 0` test that returns a Skipped result when no public key is configured, and the console never configures one — it sets only the vendor-type profile and a /tmp repository cache, and the verifier request carries no key field — so opts.PublicKeys is always empty and the openpgp code is never executed.

CVE-2024-6538 is a server-side request forgery in the console's /api/dev-console/proxy/internet endpoint, which relayed authenticated users' arbitrary outbound HTTP requests. That endpoint is not present in the pinned 4.22.10 source: pkg/devconsole/handler.go registers only three route groups — artifacthub (hard-coded bases https://artifacthub.io/api/v1 and https://github.com), tekton-results (host derived from the in-cluster TektonResults CR / OpenShift Route, always https), and the git webhook-creation handlers. The webhook handlers do take a caller-supplied destination (the request's HostName/BaseURL), but every such URL passes validateHostURL (pkg/devconsole/webhooks/validation.go): https-only, no query/fragment/userinfo, cluster-internal hostnames (localhost, kubernetes, *.svc, *.svc.cluster.local, *.pod.cluster.local) rejected, and the resolved IPs checked against private/reserved ranges; the shared HTTP client additionally re-applies the private/reserved-IP check at dial time (ssrfDialControl), closing the DNS-rebinding window between validation and connect. The unrestricted arbitrary-URL relay the advisory describes therefore does not exist in the shipped bridge.
The build ships @octokit/request 8.4.1, which is the fixed release for the 1.x-8.x line, so the vulnerable code is not present (GHSA-rmvr-2pp2-xj38: >=1.0.0 <8.4.1 and >=9.0.0-beta.1 <9.2.1).

The build ships @octokit/request-error 5.1.1, which is the fixed release for the 1.x-5.x line, so the vulnerable code is not present. GHSA-xx4v-prfh-6cgc carries two ranges — >=1.0.0 <5.1.1 (fixed in 5.1.1) and >=6.0.0 <6.1.7 (fixed in 6.1.7) — and scanners that compare the shipped 5.1.1 against the 6.x line's 6.1.7 fix report a false positive. Verified in the shipped webpack bundle: the authorization redaction uses the patched /(?<! ) .*$/ form, not the backtracking regex.

CVE-2020-8203 is prototype pollution via attacker-controlled path arguments to lodash.set; no fixed release of the standalone lodash.set package exists (the package is frozen). It is vendored solely by @octokit/rest@16, which invokes it with its own hard-coded endpoint route strings as paths — never request- or response-derived values — in browser-executed git-import flows. The bridge server does not run this code.

CVE-2026-59880 is a 32-bit trie overflow in Immutable.List requiring collections beyond 2^31 elements. The verdict rests on exploitability alone: Lists in the console are built from rendered Kubernetes API data and cannot approach that size, and the code runs only in the viewer's browser (the bridge server never executes it). As with CVE-2026-59879 the fix exists only in the immutable 4.x/5.x majors while upstream pins ^3.8.3, but that does not factor into the verdict.

CVE-2026-59879 is a hash-collision algorithmic-complexity DoS in Immutable.Map/Set. The verdict rests on exploitability alone: the library runs only in the browser bundle (the bridge server never executes it), and its Map/Set collections are built from Kubernetes API objects in the viewer's own cluster, which cannot practically supply the volume of colliding keys the attack needs — worst case is degraded rendering in that viewer's browser session, recoverable by reload. Remediation availability is orthogonal: upstream pins immutable ^3.8.3 and the fix exists only in the 4.x/5.x majors, so no 3.x-compatible bump exists, but the not_affected posture does not depend on that.

CVE-2026-50195 allows local image tag poisoning through containerd's CRI checkpoint import (pkg/cri). It is patched only in the containerd/v2 module; no 1.x fix exists. The console vendors github.com/containerd/containerd only for registry-client packages (content, images, remotes/docker); pkg/cri is not vendored, so the vulnerable code is not present in the bridge binary. Kept although GHSA-cvxm-645q-p574 lists only the containerd/v2 module (so GHSA-fed scanners never match this v1 PURL): the Go vulndb alias GO-2026-5338 marks github.com/containerd/containerd v1 as affected from 0 with no fixed version, so module-level OSV matching (osv-scanner, trivy, govulncheck -scan module) flags this PURL - an OSV /v1/query for the module at 1.7.33 returns exactly this advisory and its two siblings. Symbol-level govulncheck does not reach the vulnerable code, which is this statement's justification.

CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
